note: Long-lived API tokens for unattended clients — an AI/MCP client such as Claude Code, or a script or CI job calling the REST API. A token acts as the account that owns it: disabling or deleting that account stops the token, and its role is capped at the owner's current role. It is shown once at creation; only its hash is stored.
unavailable: Managing API tokens requires the admin role.
signInPrompt: Sign in as an admin to manage API tokens.
empty: No API tokens yet. Create one to give an AI/MCP or API client access.

field.name: Name
field.roleHint: Use Viewer for a read-only client. A token can never exceed its owner's role.
field.surfacesHint: A token reaches only the surfaces named here.
field.expiryHint: A bounded life limits what a leaked token can do.
field.ownerHint: Prefer a service account for anything unattended, so the token outlives whoever created it.
field.scopeHint: The token sees only these groups and everything beneath them.
field.scopeAllHint: Nothing selected — the token sees the whole fleet.
field.scopeNoGroups: No node groups exist yet, so this token sees the whole fleet.
field.scopeInherited: This owner is limited to node groups, and the token sees exactly what the owner sees. To give a token a narrower view, own it with a service account scoped to what it should see.

surfaceHint.mcp: The AI tool surface at /mcp — monitoring queries plus a few audited actions.
surfaceHint.rest: The northbound API, subject to the token's role. It cannot administer users.

stateHint.expired: Past its expiry, so it no longer authenticates.
stateHint.no-owner: The account that owned this token is gone, so it no longer authenticates. Revoke it to tidy the list.
stateHint.owner-disabled: The owning account is disabled, so it no longer authenticates.

ssoIdle: This token's owner signs in through SSO. Yagra is never told when an identity provider disables an account, so an SSO-owned token stops working once its owner has been absent too long — the owner's silence is the only signal there is.
